generatedProse.concept-context: Two students can work equally hard for very different reasons. Performance motivation is the drive to earn the grade and prove you are able; learning, or mastery, motivation is the drive to understand the subject for its own sake. Both fuel effort, but they part ways under pressure, and in any field the most interesting questions are often the hard ones, so which drive is stronger matters.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two students each choose a topic for the same open essay.

{{learner-a}} picks the safest, most familiar topic, the one most likely to earn a high mark with least risk. The harder, more interesting question is left alone in case it goes wrong. The essay is competent and the mark is fine, but {{learner-a}} has learned little that is new. This is performance motivation: the drive is the grade and how it looks.

{{learner-b}} is drawn to the harder question because it is the one worth understanding, even though it carries more risk. {{learner-b}} struggles with it, reads widely, and comes away understanding something genuinely new. The mark matters, but it is not the main point. This is learning, or mastery, motivation.

Both students wrote a good essay. Only {{learner-b}} chose the task for what could be learned from it.
generatedProse.summary: Performance motivation is the drive to perform well in front of others; learning (mastery) motivation is the drive to understand the subject for its own sake. Both fuel effort, but they part ways under pressure: learning motivation is more likely to take a hard topic on. You can now tell the two apart and recognise them in how a student studies. With a clear sense of what excelling is, the mindset behind it and the motivation that drives it, you have the foundations to start well.

check.body: In the worked example, what showed that {{learner-b}} was driven by learning motivation?

feedback.correct: That's right. Taking on the harder question to understand it is learning motivation.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the choice made for understanding rather than for the safe mark.
